title: Long-horizon research stays bounded by an acceptance gate
subtitle: Agents can explore longer, but environment, evidence, evaluation, and human acceptance stay explicit.

nodes.label: Research question
nodes.detail: A meaningful problem starts the investigation

nodes.label: Bounded environment
nodes.detail: Tools, data, and operating constraints define the workspace

nodes.label: Agent exploration
nodes.detail: Long-running work tests paths and can be redirected

nodes.label: Evidence review
nodes.detail: Quality and significance are checked before human acceptance

nodes.label: Human acceptance
nodes.detail: A responsible reviewer decides whether evidence is sufficient

nodes.label: Controlled use
nodes.detail: Accepted findings inform work without becoming unquestioned fact

callouts.label: Steerability
callouts.detail: The research path can be redirected when evidence is weak.

callouts.label: Evaluation
callouts.detail: Quality criteria are defined before plausible output is trusted.

callouts.label: Acceptance
callouts.detail: Human judgment remains the final boundary for consequential use.

footer: Autonomy scales research effort; evaluation and human acceptance preserve responsibility.
